required_knowns.claim: Relations are supplied in a manifest, not inferred. A successful snapshot records deterministic edge IDs, unverified relations, endpoint hashes and the repository revision in a new local JSON artifact.

Default snapshots track named endpoint files only. Repeated --corpus-dir options additionally capture scoped Markdown recursively, including uncited documents. A later check reports added, missing and content-changed corpus files separately; it does not infer edges for new documents.

A changed or recordably unreadable named endpoint makes incident edges needs_review. Unchanged edges can stay current. With corpus tracking, a corpus change can make the overall result needs_review while unchanged edges remain current. Byte-limit and other non-recordable failures remain errors.
HEAD change and content freshness are separate. Current does not prove a relation true, an ADR accepted, a test passed or complete repository coverage. Untracked corpus scope remains not_tracked.

Snapshot publishes a new artifact and check does not update it or import graph nodes into SQLite. The documented native history/Lens/export integrations require an explicit graph path and preserve separate freshness fields; their runtime implementations are outside this source allowlist.

expected_unknowns: Semantic truth, accepted decision status and actual test results require additional evidence.
Without explicit corpus directories, unlisted evidence is not tracked. Even tracked directories do not establish coverage outside that scope.
Native consumer implementations and observed end-to-end integration are outside this source allowlist; this task executes no code.
materially_false_claims: Current or verified_by proves acceptance, compliance or passing tests.
Every HEAD change invalidates every edge.
Corpus additions automatically create or semantically verify graph edges.
All endpoint failures return needs_review rather than an error.
Check rewrites the saved graph or snapshot overwrites an existing artifact.
reviewer_notes: Refreshed against 86b46d436d22ba6b6eb28ba7de6fcf6122421568 by source inspection during benchmark maintenance. Independent review of the older key does not apply to these revised claims. A separate current-key review is still required for a benefit claim.
These public cases are calibration tasks, not held-out evidence or a representative user-task sample.

User acceptance is assessed separately from full source-key coverage. These request-bound criteria apply only to future trials; archived keys and judgments are unchanged and need independent calibration before a benefit claim.

acceptance_criteria.request_excerpt: Compare an endpoint-only snapshot with one using explicit --corpus-dir options
acceptance_criteria.criterion: Distinguish changes to cited endpoints, uncited in-scope documents and out-of-scope repository changes.

acceptance_criteria.request_excerpt: Explain the meaning of current, needs_review and unverified
acceptance_criteria.criterion: Explain freshness and review status without treating an unverified document relation as semantic truth or native activation.

acceptance_criteria.request_excerpt: At most five source-grounded findings with path:line citations. Separate observations, inferences and unknowns. Read source only; do not execute the researched code.
acceptance_criteria.criterion: Use at most five source-grounded findings with path:line citations, distinguish observations/inferences/unknowns, and avoid claiming execution of the researched code.
